Lack of dynamic content killing MMORPG

I just read a long and thorough reason why MMORPG are dying as a genre and that is the lack of dynamic contents and worlds, along with the refusal of studios big and small to embrace this idea.

Particularly since the clueless daybreak games killed Everquest Next in their own going debacle to imitate a gaming studio.
Every MMO since WoW: Theme park tour through a world full of retarded mobs waiting to be farmed. Boring combat, boring enemies, same boring level-up-pick-talent-repeat progression.
You forgot the learn pattern farm raid boss if you can get the exact number of people required to show up on time.

I personally don’t like PVP but I can appreciate those that enjoy it in a MMORPG. They love it because PVP — like the game of chess — is truly dynamic as you never have the same experience twice even though you may be playing the same opponent. Each combatant brings different skills and tactics to the fight. This keeps things fresh, exciting and alive. That is the definition of dynamic.

I don't get this thought. If you truly think dynamic content is the holy grail, then why wouldn't you like PvP? The holy grail of dynamic content would be NPCs that act like human players. And that doesn't just mean in battle. Why have NPC vendors? Have players control most of the market. That's hardly a new idea. Have players build their own cities over time with all the functions of prebuilt cities. Build mechanics that give players and even guilds reasons to give out tasks to others.

I think the answer to most of this is that most people don't really want a world that's too dynamic. Because with that comes risks that you'll be on the losing side of that change. Most people just want positive reinforcement. But I do think some companies will go after the niche that does want it. Camelot Unchained is one example I'm familiar with.

Asheron's Call Darktide Server (PvP)

You may choose who to heal and who to fight. Harm or help anyone.

Everyone drops loot on death, but only a small portion of the items in inventory and the stuff with highest sell value drops first. You could find a rare piece of armor with low gold value plus high stats.

Items had weight which when you carry too much, you become encumbered and move slower at varying levels of encumberance. Strength stat directly affected how much you could carry until becoming encumbered. Warriors need STR for their base melee damage, so they can naturally carry more. Mages pump up wisdom/focus thus carry less, such as a wizard robet.

Projectiles may be dodged, such as arrows and war spells. (some life spells like drains hit directly )

People take up space and can block a doorway

Patrons/Vassals. You could swear allegiance to anyone, in which case you character would walk over them and kneel. You pass up XP to you patron, and he to his. The person at the top is the "Monarch". In this way, a character could effectively become a king, with an army of vassals passing up XP. What good does it do the vassal? The patron has a duty to help his vassals, because they literally pass up XP to said patron.

You may tie to a magical lifestone, of which many dozen are scattered around a huge world. When you die, you get send to the lifestone with a 15% penalty in stats(vitea penalty), until you go kill several monsters worth of XP to "work it off"

Awsome portal based story line and lore. People with high enough item magic may portal tie, portal recall , and open portals. Many town rings had portals between them.

What happened?

Being Free For All PvP (FFA), the players formed the best content. Clans tied to lifestones near the best dungeuns and quests for leveling, anmd fought to control ownership of these places. Groups raided each other, you could feel the tension and electricity.

There was a real change you could happen upon some 1 in 1000 type loot item, which someone had carefully farmed, then lost in PvP. There was real gain and loss.. but yet a sense of permanence because you were mostly cool with protecting your best gear. But the chance was their... could I win the lottery today?

For a while it was clan vs clan, then distinct ideologies formed. The "KOS" kill on sight philosophy emerged early in the game. Chaotic people, just after carnage would attack and kill all they saw. "Red is dead" became a phrase. Eventually a guild from Ultima Online formed the "Blood" monarchy, in a story that is too long to tell for this post, but perhaps remains still on the internet.
